info.text:
In a 2026 Bankrate survey, just 38% of couples fully merged their money.
36% mix joint and separate accounts; 26% keep everything separate. Among Gen Z (18-29), 51% keep money completely separate.
Census data: married couples with no joint account rose from 15% in 1996 to 23% in 2023.
Hypothetical income split: $6,000 and $4,000 a month sharing $3,000 in bills = $1,800 and $1,200, and both keep 70% of pay. The FDIC insures joint accounts up to $250,000 per co-owner, per bank.
Sources: Bankrate/YouGov couples survey (Dec 2025 fieldwork, published Feb 2026); US Census Bureau SIPP (Sept 2025); FDIC.
News and education, not financial advice.
Follow @financeprostv for money explained simply.
